newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: PLO in bid to block extradition of Hamas leader.
newsitem.headline: PLO in bid to block extradition of Hamas leader.

text.p: The Palestinian Authority is seeking to block the extradition to Israel of the U.S.-held political leader of the militant Moslem group Hamas, a top PLO official said on Monday.

Mahmoud Abbas, the Palestinian architect of peace deals with Israel, told Reuters the Palestinian Authority (PA) was doing its best to ensure Hamas leader Mousa Abu Marzouk is extradited to Palestinian self-rule areas or to any Arab country.

"The PA is exerting efforts so that Abu Marzouk is not handed over to Israel because this will only complicate matters," added Abbas, a close aide to Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat who is on an official visit to the United Arab Emirates.
Hamas has warned of guerrilla attacks should Abu Marzouk be sent to the Jewish state, the movement's avowed enemy.
"The PA has made a request to the U.S. administration to return Abu Marzouk to his country," said Abbas, known as Abu Mazen.
"If he is to be extradited, let him be handed over to the PA and returned to his country. If this is impossible, then we welcome his extradition to any Arab country."

Abu Marzouk, a native of the Gaza Strip which is ruled by the PA, has been held in New York since immigration officials detained him in July 1995 after arriving in the United States, where he had lived for at least 15 years.
Israel said it wanted Washington to extradite him to stand trial for alleged responsibility for Hamas attacks which killed scores of Israelis.
Abu Marzouk's lawyers said last month he had decided to withdraw an appeal against his extradition. His decision means that he can be handed over to Israel within about 60 days.
He had said he was involved only in Hamas political matters for which he could not be extradited.

Israeli security sources have said Israeli officials, fearing violent protests if Abu Marzouk ended up in an Israeli jail, were examining a deal with U.S. and Jordanian officials to send him to Jordan in return for a pledge to shun violence.
Abu Marzouk said in an interview with an Israeli newspaper published last week he would agree to be sent to another country instead of Israel.
Jordan expelled Abu Marzouk in June 1995 to help improve ties with Israel and the PA.
